I was 16 and my older cousin, who was 20, gave me LSD at a family barbecue at his parents' place. He said it would be fun and that he'd look after me. I'd never taken anything before except a bit of weed. For the first hour I felt giggly and the colours were nice. Then my aunt called everyone to the table and I had to sit there with the whole family, my parents, my grandparents, my little sister. The food started to move on the plate. The meat looked alive. My grandfather's face kept changing, sometimes old, sometimes young, sometimes like a skull. I couldn't follow the conversation, people were asking me questions about school and I didn't know how to answer.

I became terrified that my parents would find out. Then I became terrified that I'd broken my brain and would be like this forever, and that my life was over at 16. I went to the bathroom and locked the door and looked in the mirror and didn't recognise my own face. My cousin came and knocked and told me to come out and act normal. He sounded annoyed, not worried. I didn't come out for an hour. My mum knocked and asked if I was sick and I said I had a stomach ache.

We went home and I lay in my bed all night with my eyes open, watching the ceiling crawl, sure that I was going insane. I had school the next morning and I went because I was afraid that staying home would make my parents suspicious. I sat through classes still feeling strange, everything too loud and too bright. I didn't tell anyone for years.

Ich war mit zwei Freunden im Park und wir hatten Pilze genommen. Mitten im Trip kam eine Polizeikontrolle. Ich musste meinen Ausweis zeigen und Fragen beantworten und konnte kaum sprechen. Die Polizisten haben gemerkt, dass etwas nicht stimmt, und uns durchsucht. Sie haben nichts gefunden, aber ich hatte panische Angst, verhaftet zu werden. Die Uniformen und das Blaulicht haben sich in meinem Kopf zu etwas Bedrohlichem verwandelt, als wäre ich in einem Kriegsgebiet.

I booked a five-day 'transformational' retreat in the Netherlands that combined daily breathwork sessions with three truffle ceremonies. I was in a stable place in my life and I went mostly out of curiosity and for personal growth. Looking back, the schedule was intense: up at 6am for cold plunges and breathwork, ceremony every other day, very little sleep, a lot of sharing circles in the evenings that went until midnight.

The first ceremony was beautiful. I felt a lot of love, cried about my grandmother, and felt connected to the group. The facilitators praised me in the sharing circle for being 'so open'.

The second ceremony was two days later, after two nights of maybe four hours of sleep. They gave a higher dose. This time I went somewhere very big. I felt that I was receiving messages about my purpose. I understood that I had a special role to play, that I had been chosen to bring a new kind of consciousness into the world. I felt incredibly powerful and also very responsible. When I came out of the ceremony, the feeling didn't go away. I couldn't sleep that night at all. My thoughts were racing. I felt I could see connections between everything, people's names, the patterns on the wallpaper, the timing of birdsong. I wrote pages and pages in my notebook.

The next day in the breathwork session I hyperventilated, as instructed, and I went into a state where I was laughing and crying at the same time and shouting. The facilitators said this was a breakthrough. I told the group in the circle that evening that I was a vessel for a higher intelligence and that I knew things about each of them. I think I said some quite intrusive things to people. Some of them looked frightened. One of the facilitators took me aside and said that maybe I should skip the third ceremony. I was furious, I thought they were jealous of my awakening.

That night I didn't sleep again. I walked around the grounds in the dark, talking to the trees. I was convinced that the stars were sending me signals. Around 4am I knocked on the facilitators' door to tell them I'd understood the secret of time. They looked very worried.

In the morning they told me that it was best for me to leave the retreat. They didn't call a doctor. They drove me to the train station and gave me back part of my money. I don't think they wanted any trouble. I had to travel home alone, by train and plane, in what I now know was a manic state. At the airport I was talking to strangers about my mission, I missed my flight because I got lost in the duty-free looking for 'signs', and I was crying and laughing in the bathroom. A security officer noticed me and called a medic, who asked me some questions and then let me go when I calmed down for a moment. I eventually got a later flight.

When I arrived home my partner picked me up and immediately knew something was very wrong. She took me to the emergency room the next day. I didn't think I needed help; I thought I was enlightened. It took a few days before I could see that something was not right with my mind. The crash came about a week later.

I was visiting my parents for the holidays and took LSD with a cannabis edible in the evening, after they'd gone to bed. I thought it would be cosy. Instead time completely broke down. I'd look at the clock and it would say 11:42, then I'd do a few things and look again and it would still say 11:42, or it would say 11:41. I became convinced that the drugs had damaged my brain and that I'd lost the ability to experience time normally, that I'd be stuck in this stretched-out moment forever. I kept walking from room to room, trying not to wake my parents. When the sun finally came up I cried from relief.

I'd been reading a lot about ayahuasca and decided to make my own version at home with Syrian rue (an MAOI) and DMT extract. I followed a guide from an internet forum. I'd been told to avoid certain foods, and I thought I had. I didn't realise that the cold medicine I'd taken the day before could also interact.

About 30 minutes after drinking the rue, I took the DMT. The visions came on slowly and they were very beautiful at first, jungle colours, a sense of being welcomed. Then I got a crushing headache, worse than any headache I've ever had, like my skull was being split. My heart was pounding so hard I could see my shirt moving. I started vomiting and couldn't stop. I knew something was medically wrong but I was too deep in the visions to think clearly. The visions turned dark: I saw blood vessels bursting, red explosions behind my eyes. I was convinced I was having a stroke and that I was going to die alone in my apartment.

I managed to call a friend who lived nearby. She came and found me on the bathroom floor and called an ambulance. My blood pressure was dangerously high. At the hospital they treated me for a hypertensive reaction. The doctors were angry with me, one of them said I was lucky not to have had a brain haemorrhage. I spent the night in the ER, still seeing patterns and feeling like I was going to die every time my heart skipped.

Ich habe im Rahmen einer Behandlung gegen Depressionen Ketamin-Infusionen in einer Klinik bekommen. Bei der dritten Infusion ist etwas schiefgelaufen, oder zumindest hat es sich so angefühlt. Ich hatte das Gefühl, mein Körper ist verschwunden und ich bin tot. Ich konnte nicht schreien, nicht sprechen, nichts. Ich war in einem leeren grauen Raum ohne Zeit. Als es vorbei war, hat die Pflegekraft nur gefragt, ob alles okay ist, und gesagt, das sei normal.

I took a high dose of 1P-LSD, maybe 250-300ug, by myself on a Saturday and decided to walk around the city because I thought it would be interesting. For a while it was. Then I went down into the subway because the noise outside was too much, and it was a terrible decision. The fluorescent lights were flickering and everyone on the platform looked like they were made of plastic, with blank, identical faces. I became convinced that everyone around me was a robot, that I was the last real human being, and that if they found out I was human they'd do something to me. I got on a train just to get away and rode it to the end of the line.

When I got out I was in a part of the city I didn't know at all. My phone battery was dead. It was getting dark. I was walking around for hours, trying to find my way back, and every street looked the same. I was crying and talking to myself. People were crossing the street to avoid me. At one point I sat down on a bench and a homeless man sat next to me and asked if I was alright. I told him that everyone was robots and he laughed in a kind way and said 'yeah, sometimes it feels like that'. He stayed with me for a long time and shared his tea from a thermos. He told me about his life. Eventually he walked me to a bus stop and told me which bus to take. I don't know his name. I think about him a lot.

I've been taking lithium for bipolar disorder for six years. I didn't know at the time that lithium combined with psychedelics can cause seizures. I took about 1.5g of mushrooms at a friend's place. Around 40 minutes in I felt a strange jolt through my body, then my vision went white. The next thing I remember is waking up on the floor with paramedics around me, a terrible headache and blood in my mouth from biting my tongue. My friend said I'd been convulsing for about two minutes. I was still tripping in the ambulance, and the sirens and the lights were horrible. I had no idea what had happened and thought I'd died and come back.

Ich hatte bei Freunden Pilze genommen. Irgendwann war ich überzeugt, dass alle meine Gedanken laut hörbar sind und dass alle wissen, was ich denke. Ich habe mich furchtbar geschämt und mich in eine Ecke gesetzt.

This happened about three years ago. I'm going to describe it in detail because I think the details matter.

Three friends and I rented a cabin in the mountains for a long weekend. Two of us, me and my friend J, had experience with LSD. The other two had only done mushrooms once. We planned to take LSD on Saturday, with one person staying sober, but on the day everyone wanted to take it, and the sober-sitter idea was abandoned. In hindsight that was the first mistake. We each took about 200ug around 2pm.

The afternoon was great. We hiked down to the lake, lay on the rocks, watched the clouds. The two less-experienced friends were giggling and having a great time. J was quieter than usual, but I didn't think much of it. I was having a beautiful trip, feeling very connected to nature.

Around sunset, things started to change with J. He began saying that he could hear the lake speaking to him. At first we thought he was joking. Then he started saying that the lake wanted him, that he had to go to it. He was staring at the water and wouldn't respond to us. His eyes looked completely different, like there was nobody behind them. I tried to talk to him and he suddenly pushed me away, hard, and shouted that I was one of 'them'. I didn't know who 'them' was.

I was still very high, and his behaviour sent my own trip into a nightmare. The sunset turned blood red. The trees around the lake looked like they were leaning in to watch. I felt that something evil had come for J and that it would come for me next. The other two were panicking and crying. One of them said we should call for help, but there was no signal at the lake.

J then walked straight into the lake with his clothes on. It was early autumn and the water was freezing. He kept walking until he was up to his chest, and then he started swimming out towards the middle. I don't really know how I made the decision, but I went in after him. The cold hit me like a wall. On LSD it felt like I was being stabbed with a thousand knives, and I felt my body dissolving into the black water. I lost the sense of where I ended and the lake began. For a moment I genuinely didn't know if I was alive. I remember thinking very clearly: this is how I die.

Somehow I reached him. He was thrashing and shouting, and he hit me in the face. I grabbed his jacket and started pulling him back. I don't know how long it took. It felt like hours. When we got to the shore, the other two pulled us out. J was shaking and blue-lipped and kept mumbling about the voice in the water. I couldn't stop shaking either. One of the others ran up to the cabin to find signal and call emergency services.

Waiting for them was the worst part. It was dark by then. We wrapped J in every blanket and jacket we had. He alternated between staring blankly and screaming that we were trying to kill him. At one point he tried to run back to the water and we had to hold him down. Holding a friend down while he screams at you, while you're on LSD and the world is melting, is something I will never forget. I felt like a monster. I felt like I was in a horror film. I was also convinced, part of the time, that maybe he was right, maybe we were the bad guys and I just didn't know it.

The mountain rescue arrived after about an hour and a half with a police car and an ambulance. The lights and the uniforms made everything worse. They separated us and asked us questions. I couldn't make sense of their words. They took J away in the ambulance, sedated. They checked me for hypothermia and let me stay at the cabin with the others, but a police officer stayed with us for a while and took our details. I kept asking if J would be okay and nobody could tell me.

The rest of the night, the three of us sat in the cabin with all the lights on. Nobody slept. The LSD was still going and every sound outside sounded like footsteps. I kept seeing J's face, his empty eyes. I kept feeling the cold water closing over my head. I felt that something had broken in the world.

J was in a psychiatric ward for three weeks. He had a psychotic episode that lasted well beyond the trip. He's mostly okay now, but our friendship has never been the same. He doesn't remember most of that night, and I remember all of it.

At a retreat in Peru I was offered kambo (frog poison) in the morning before an ayahuasca ceremony in the evening. Nobody explained the risks properly. The kambo made me vomit and my face swelled up and I felt like I was suffocating. My heart was racing and I lay on the ground for an hour unable to move. I was still weak in the evening but they said the ceremony would 'complete the cleansing'. The ayahuasca hit me very hard because I was dehydrated and exhausted. I saw myself as a corpse being eaten by insects. I couldn't get up to go to the toilet and soiled myself. I felt utterly humiliated and terrified. Nobody came to help me until morning.

Ich war mit einer Freundin auf Reisen in Thailand und wir sind zu einer Full-Moon-Party gegangen. Dort hat uns jemand Pilz-Shakes verkauft, und ich habe einen ganzen getrunken, ohne zu wissen, wie stark er ist. Nach einer Stunde war ich völlig weg. Die Musik, die Feuer-Shows, die tausend Menschen am Strand, alles hat sich zu einem Albtraum vermischt. Ich habe meine Freundin verloren und bin am Strand umhergeirrt. Irgendwann habe ich bemerkt, dass meine Tasche weg war, mit Pass, Geld und Handy. Ich hatte panische Angst, nie wieder nach Hause zu kommen. Dann kamen zwei Männer in Uniform, ich weiß nicht, ob es echte Polizisten waren, und haben mich gefragt, ob ich Drogen genommen habe. Sie haben gedroht, mich ins Gefängnis zu bringen, wenn ich nicht bezahle. Ich hatte kein Geld. Sie haben mich eine Weile festgehalten und angeschrien, bis sie mich irgendwann gehen ließen. Ich habe bis zum Morgen hinter einem Boot gesessen und gezittert. Meine Freundin hat mich am nächsten Tag gefunden.
